examples: ['Turn 1 states that the old senatorial factions have been abolished, yet Turn 3 describes a faction of senators staging a coup, implying those factions still exist.', 'Turn 8 says the plague killed the emperor and his heir, but then decrees a new emperor who is described as “his young, untested son,” suggesting an heir survived despite the claim that the heir was dead.']

['Turn\u202f3 describes the Praetorian Guard as “wary” after a brutal crackdown on the Senate mutiny, yet Turn\u202f8 has the Guard actively backing Julius\u202fOrestes in a decisive march to demand the imperial throne, implying a level of confidence and cohesion that contradicts their earlier wariness.']

['Turn\u202f6 says “Emperor Arcadius … extends a modest trade concession to the Eastern Empire,” which contradicts earlier statements that Arcadius is the Eastern emperor offering concessions to the Western Empire; an emperor cannot grant a concession to his own empire.', 'Turn\u202f8 treats Romulus Augustus as having abdicated and installs a new emperor, yet throughout Turns\u202f1‑7 there is no indication of his abdication or any crisis that would lead to his removal, making the succession claim inconsistent with the previously stable reign.']

['Turn1 claims the Senate has crumbled and its doors remain closed, yet Turn8 has the Senate formally ratify the succession edict, implying it still functions.', 'Turn1 states Rome is no longer plagued by whispers of coup or civil war, but Turn3 reveals a discovered conspiracy with ringleaders that needed to be executed.']

['Turn\u202f3 portrays the Senate as already subdued and stripped of its rebellious core, but Turn\u202f8 refers to the Senate as "fractious," implying it is still openly dissenting.', 'Turn\u202f2 shows the Eastern court quietly mobilizing its navy out of wariness toward Rome’s resurgence, yet Turn\u202f8 states the Eastern court "accepts" Romulus Augustus’s nomination, suggesting a cooperative stance that contradicts the earlier suspicion.']
